title.narrative: GH-Legal Reform and Legal Aid for the Advancement of Women

description.narrative: Legal reform can improve gender equality and establish a supportive institutional environment, by reforming isntitutions to establish equal rights and opportunities for women and men, fostering incentives for more equal resources and participation, and redressing disparities in access to resources. Engendering Development Through Gender Equality in Rights, Resources, and Voice, The World Bank and Oxford University Press, 2001. This IDF proposal is aimed at supporting current efforts, from both government and civil society, to launch a gender-responsive legal reform process. It is proposed to achieve this through: 1. Providing the Attorney-General's Offices and the Ministry for Women and Children's Affairs' technical staff with the skills needed to successfully carry out its mandate through the acquisition of stronger management, advocacy and strategic alliance/partnership building techniques at both central and regional level. 2. Strengthening the capacity of the Ministry of Justice in leading the techinical team in charge of the launch of the following three components: (a) identification of gender-discriminatory provisions in the national constitiution, national and state statutes and regulations, religious law, customary law and paractice, and court deisions; (b) drafting of new gender-responsive legislation, and (c) carrying out of legal literacy initiatives. 3. Building on the existing partnership between Government and civil society in extending the outreach of legal and judicial aid program through a more comprehensive and innovative approach to legal and judicial aid.
